I completed my Bachelor’s degree in Biology at Heinrich Heine University where I first came into contact with marine biology during an exchange semester in Tromsø, Norway. I subsequently started a Master’s degree in Marine Biology at the University of Rostock and spent a semester at Memorial University in St. John’s, Canada. For my Master’s thesis  I investigated the biodiversity of Brittle Stars in the North Atlantic with the benthic biology group. Following this I started a PhD position in collaboration with Nord University in Bodø, Norway.

Living in the Arctic, I am particularly interested in the rapid environmental changes occurring both on land and in the ocean. My research focuses on brittle stars in the North Atlantic and Arctic Ocean with a special emphasis on taxonomy and population connectivity. 

The sampling efforts within the ALONGate project allows me to investigate population dynamics of selected species, analyse their geographic range expansions, and gain insights into their ecology.
